title: Reduction tower from an integral lattice is normalized
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell
e p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n$ for $n\geq1$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme and $X=X_0	imes_{k_0}k$. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ use the completed coefficient sheaf $R_X=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,X}=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X$ and its quotient projections of [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $K_{\mathcal O}\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$ be an integral object of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and suppose its derived reductions $K_n=K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$ of [def-weil-integral-derived-reduction] lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ for all $n$. Give these reductions the quotient-induced transitions of [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower], regarded as $t_{n+1,n}:K_{n+1}	o r_{n+1,n}K_n$ in $D(X,A_{n+1})$, where $r_{n+1,n}$ is restriction of scalars as in [def-trf-adic-system].

For every $n\geq j\geq1$, the map adjoint to the composite transition $t_{n,j}$ is the canonical derived associativity isomorphism
$$

u_{n,j}:K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_j\xrightarrow{\sim}K_{\mathcal O}\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_j)_X=K_j.$$
These are the actual adjoints of the quotient transitions, with $
u_{n,n}=1$ and $
u_{n,i}=
u_{j,i}\circ(
u_{n,j}\otimes^L_{A_j}A_i)$ under derived associativity for $n\geq j\geq i$. Thus the reduction tower with these transitions is a normalized $A_ ullet$-system in the sense of [def-trf-adic-system].

proof.text: Write $R=R_X$ and $B_n=(A_n)_X$. By [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], choose a quasi-isomorphism $P\to K_{\mathcal O}$ with $P$ K-flat over $R$ and flat in every degree. In [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] use this choice, so $P_n=P\otimes_R B_n$ represents $K_n$ and the adjacent transitions are $\mathrm{id}_P\otimes\rho_{n+1,n}$. For $n\geq j$, their composite is the chain map $\tau_{n,j}(x\otimes a)=x\otimes\rho_{n,j}(a)$, by composing the adjacent quotient maps. This is $B_n$-linear with the target restricted along $\rho_{n,j}$, since $\pi_j=\rho_{n,j}\pi_n$, and therefore represents the specified $t_{n,j}$ before forgetting to $D(R)$. For $j=n$ it is the identity.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] to the sheaf-ring map $R\to B_n$ on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. Its hypotheses hold because Step 1 chose both K-flatness and flat terms. Thus $P_n$ is K-flat over $B_n$ and has flat terms. By [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $K_n\otimes^L_{B_n}B_j$ is computed by $P_n\otimes_{B_n}B_j$, and $K_j$ is computed by $P\otimes_R B_j$. These computations use the same $P$ for every index and are canonical under changes of K-flat resolution. No flatness of $R\to B_n$ or $B_n\to B_j$ is asserted or needed.

proof.text: On these models let $\alpha_{n,j}:(P\otimes_R B_n)\otimes_{B_n}B_j\to P\otimes_R B_j$ be the $B_j$-linear map whose adjunct under the ordinary extension/restriction adjunction along $\rho_{n,j}$ [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction] is the $B_n$-linear map $\tau_{n,j}$ of Step 1; on local sections $(x\otimes a)\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes\rho_{n,j}(a)b$. Let $\beta_{n,j}$ be the $B_j$-linear map whose adjunct along $\pi_j$ is the $R$-linear map $P\to(P\otimes_RB_n)\otimes_{B_n}B_j$, $x\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes1$; it is $R$-linear because $\pi_j=\rho_{n,j}\pi_n$ and the balancing relations of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] give $(xr\otimes1)\otimes1=(x\otimes1)\otimes\pi_j(r)$. By uniqueness of adjuncts, $\alpha\beta=1$ since $\alpha\beta(x\otimes1)=x\otimes1$, and $\beta\alpha=1$ since both are $B_j$-linear and, after the unit $z\mapsto z\otimes1$, are $B_n$-linear maps out of $P\otimes_RB_n$ agreeing on $x\otimes1$. Naturality of the adjunction makes $\alpha,\beta$ chain maps (the differential is $d\otimes1$). The same construction applies with any K-flat flat-term complex over any of the rings in place of $P$ over $R$. Thus $\alpha_{n,j}$ represents the change-of-rings composition (associativity) isomorphism $\nu_{n,j}$ on the models of Step 2.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product; elementary mixed-ring balancing calculation

proof.text: Use the derived extension/restriction adjunction of [def-sfb-derived-extend-restrict-adjunction] in the category of abelian sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$, as [def-trf-adic-system] specifies; that node verifies the Grothendieck, closed symmetric monoidal, additive tensor and functorial flat-resolution hypotheses, and restriction of scalars is exact. Its module objects over $B_n$, $B_j$ are the sheaves of modules and its relative tensor product is the sheaf tensor product, so $L\operatorname{Ext}$ is the derived change of rings of Step 2, and the derived adjunction is the one induced by the ordinary adjunction [def-sfb-modobj-extend-restrict-adjunction]: on a K-flat complex with flat terms its unit is the class of the ordinary unit $z\mapsto z\otimes1$. This is the normalization of [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction] for $\rho_{n,j}:B_n\to B_j$ (same functors, same unit, hence the same adjunction), whose clause (2) says: for the morphism of complexes $\tau_{n,j}:P_n\to\operatorname{Res}P_j$, the adjunct of its class is the class of $P_n\otimes_{B_n}B_j\to P_j$, $z\otimes b\mapsto b\,\tau_{n,j}(z)$, which is $\alpha_{n,j}$ of Step 3. Hence the map adjoint to the specified transition $t_{n,j}=[\tau_{n,j}]$ of Step 1 is $\nu_{n,j}$, an isomorphism; it is the actual adjoint, not a chosen isomorphism with the same endpoints.

For $n\geq j\geq i$: by [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] applied to $P_n$ along $\rho_{n,j}$, the complex $P_n\otimes_{B_n}B_j$ is again K-flat with flat terms over $B_j$, so by [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] $(K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_j)\otimes^L_{A_j}A_i$ is computed by $(P_n\otimes_{B_n}B_j)\otimes_{B_j}B_i$, and $\nu_{n,j}\otimes^L_{A_j}A_i$ by $\alpha_{n,j}\otimes1$. The associativity identification with $K_n\otimes^L_{A_n}A_i$ is the map of Step 3 with $P_n$ over $B_n$ in place of $P$ over $R$: $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c\mapsto(x\otimes a)\otimes\rho_{j,i}(b)c$. Following it by $\alpha_{n,i}$, and alternatively applying $\alpha_{n,j}\otimes1$ then $\alpha_{j,i}$, both send $((x\otimes a)\otimes b)\otimes c$ to $x\otimes\rho_{n,i}(a)\rho_{j,i}(b)c$, using $\rho_{j,i}\rho_{n,j}=\rho_{n,i}$; as all maps are $B_i$-linear and determined by these values (uniqueness of adjuncts as in Step 3), the cocycle equation holds on models and hence in the derived category. For $n=j$, $\alpha_{n,n}$ is the unit identification $P_n\otimes_{B_n}B_n\cong P_n$, so $\nu_{n,n}=1$. The levels lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,A_n)$ by hypothesis; with Step 4 these are exactly the normalization requirements of [def-trf-adic-system].
